newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: MINISTRY TO DISCUSS LAL-LIETUVA MERGER.
newsitem.headline: MINISTRY TO DISCUSS LAL-LIETUVA MERGER.

text.p: The Lithuanian transport ministry will discuss the merger of Lithuanian Airlines (LAL) and Aviation Company Lietuva on Monday, an official at the ministry said.
"There should be a decision (today)...it must be discussed," Nerijus Stukenas, director of the transport ministry's civil aviation department, told Reuters.
"I don't know what the result will be, but I think these two companies will be joined, he said."
"It would not be a bad decision," Stukenas said. "We don't need two state airlines."
The Lithuanian government unveiled its plan to privatise the two air companies earlier this year. Both LAL and Lietuva are 100 percent state-run.
LAL has a share capital of 76.5 million litas, while the share capital of Lietuva is 2.8 million litas.
Last month Lithuania's securities commission registered a share capital boost of 1.65 million litas for Lietuva to 4.42 million litas from additional contributions.
LAL's fleet consists of three Boeing 737-200s, two Saab 340Bs, a Jetstar, five Tu-134s and 11 YAK 42s.
LAL is currently negotiating a deal to sell its YAK 42s to Pakistan's Bhoja Airline Pvt.
Lietuva's fleet consists of six YAK 40s, one Tu 134 and one ATR 42-300.
